pr_comments:
I don't have time to do a very deep dive on this, but note that this PR breaks with any sort of movement during idle processing when the physics tick rate is lower than the idle tick rate, where the transformations seem to compound in some way.

The simplest way to repro is to just set `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second` to `30`, and apply the following script to an `AnimatableBody3D`:

```gdscript
extends AnimatableBody3D

var elapsed := 0.0

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	elapsed += delta
	global_position.x = sin(elapsed)
```

Alternatively you can also animate it using an `AnimationPlayer` node, with a `position` track, while leaving the `AnimationPlayer`'s `callback_mode_process` property at the default of `ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_IDLE`.
Found out my test model was just wrong. And can't figure out the correct sequence of matrix transforms to make this work, sorry.

I guess the problem is that you can't really distinguish between a relative transformation (`position.x += delta`) and an absolute transformation (`position.x = sin(elapsed)`) with the revert approach used by `sync_to_physics`, so you're forced to assume one or the other.

In fact, the code currently seems to assume only absolute transformations, so you'll find that `position.x += delta` is currently broken when done from the idle processing, whereas I guess your PR would have fixed this but instead breaks absolute transformations.

issue_context.title: AnimatableBody2D animates only one property when sync_to_physics is enabled (using AnimationPlayer)
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.3.stable

### System information

macOS 14.6.1 - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 Pro - Apple M2 Pro (10 Threads)

### Issue description

1. I am animating a `AnimatableBody2D` using an `AnimationPlayer`
2. The `AnimatableBody2D` is not moving unless I turn **off** `sync_to_physics`
3. I tried with bezier curve animation and without, no change
4. At some point it animated at least partially, now (with no conscious change) it doesn't animate at all
5. Since it does animate with `sync_to_physics` turned off I assume it's not an error on my side

If anybody has any ideas, please. I have no clue anymore ...

**Potentially related issues:**
- #76685
- #58269

### Steps to reproduce

I am not able to reproduce it from scratch, but I extracted the problem from my larger project:
1. Open and run the project (with visible collision shapes)
2. Shape should move, but doesn't 😭
3. Turn off `sync_to_physics` on to animatable_body_2d and run scene
4. It now moves 😤

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[bug-animating-animatable-body-zip.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17681220/bug-animating-animatable-body-zip.zip)
comments: **I think I figured it out 🔥:** Multiple "channels" won't animate in parallel - A) Works ("normal" animation) - B) Glitches (position is split up into x and y when using bezier curves) - C) Works (bezier curve animation but only one axis) → Only one property will animate properly. If you add a rotation channel, then either position or rotation won't animate anymore (when using `sync_to_physics`). [bug-animating-animatable-body-alt.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17683798/bug-animating-animatable-body-alt.zip)
So it's probably the same underlying issue as @ZeAntwan encountered in  #76685

The [code seems pretty short](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e65a23762b36b564eb94672031f37fdadba72333/scene/2d/physics/animatable_body_2d.cpp#L55-L57), so maybe it's not hard to fix ... but I don't understand anything 😭

Reproduced, in animation3d too. It looks like the transform is set each frame as many times as there are tracks separately, so only the last one applies. 
Also happens, for example, if you add a 3d rotation track after adding the bezier: then only the rotation happens.

review_comments: In my uttermost ignorance of the topic, why... why does this work?

Essentially, it adds the difference.
```
diff = global - last_valid
next = next + diff
```

Shorthand
```
next += global - last_valid
```

Could also write it like this
```
next += (-last_valid) + global
```

or this
```
next += inverse(last_valid) + global
```

But these are transform matrix, need to combine them with a special * operator.
```
next = next * inverse(last_valid) * global
```
